To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DNA of the macronuclei of Tetrahymenas is extruded in large extrusion bodies, which are formed in the course of a cell cycle and which are released at cell division.

the macronuclei of Tetrahymenas are able to divide and to synthesize DNA, even in the absence of the micronuclei and that the macronuclear DNA is randomly distributed between daughter nuclei and the extrusion body.

DNA is extruded from the macronuclear genome of Tetrahymen pyriformis in a random fashion and that DNA extrusion is a mechanism to eliminate the excess amount of DNA present at the first division of a Tetrahymena cell after exposure to 5-bromouracil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) What is the fate of DNA in the macromucleus of Tet. pyriformis after inhibition of cell division by 5-bromouridine?
the regulation of cell multiplication and the mechanism of DNA replication in Tetrahymena.
the mechanism of the DNA extrusion from the macronuclear nucleus of Tetrahymen pyriformis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in Tetrahymena, the macronuclei contain the genetic information necessary for cell multiplication.
the extrusion body represents a part of the macronuclei, which is extruded from the macronuclear mass.
the extrusion body does not contain a random sample of macronuclear DNA but a random sample of the DNA in one macronucleus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the DNA in a cell is distributed in two ways during cell multiplication: (1) by random distribution between daughter nuclei, and (2) by selective distribution between daughter nuclei and a large body, which is extruded at the first division following the inhibition of DNA synthesis.
the extrusion bodies are the remnants of the macronuclei.

the macronuclei in the G2-phase of the cell cycle contain a full complement of DNA and that this DNA is randomly divided between daughter nuclei and an extrusion body at the first division following the inhibition of cell multiplication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the extrusion body contains a random sample of DNA from the nucleus.
the DNA of Tetrahymema macronuclei is not a random mixture of the DNA of all micronuclei.
the macronuclei of Tetrahymenas are able to extrude large amounts of DNA in a random way.
